indian.headline: Indian markets closed higher on broad-based gains; realty and metals led the charge.
indian.lead: Indian markets closed higher on broad-based gains; realty and metals led the charge.
indian.brief: Sensex rose 0.50% and Nifty 50 gained 0.63%, with Bank Nifty up 0.67%, as realty and metals outperformed while IT lagged.
why: Realty stocks surged 2.9%, driven by strong construction and property demand, lifting index heavyweights and broad sentiment.
Metal stocks climbed 2.8% on energy and commodity strength, signaling economic optimism and industrial activity pickup.
Banking sector gained 0.7% after SBI reported 14% jump in Q2 standalone net profit at ₹23,038 crore, boosting financial stock confidence.
IT sector fell 1.5%, acting as a drag on overall gains as tech stocks faced profit-taking pressure despite the broader rally.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities closed on an up note today as a rally in realty, metals, and energy sectors offset weakness in IT. The Sensex climbed 0.50% while Nifty 50 gained 0.63%, with Bank Nifty outperforming at 0.67%. Sector-wise, realty led with a 2.9% jump, followed by metals at 2.8% and energy at 2.2%, signaling strength in construction, commodities, and infrastructure plays. Banking stocks benefited from SBI's strong Q2 earnings—a 14% year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to ₹23,038 crore—which boosted investor confidence in the sector.

On the flip side, IT shares fell 1.5%, dragging slightly on the headline indices. Beyond the main indices, individual stock movers grabbed headlines: SFC Environmental Tech surged 12% on its second day of listing, ideaForge Technology jumped 5% after reporting its first quarterly profit in two years, and Reliance Industries rose 11.6% on strong results and heavy leveraged buying. NSE shares also gained traction after Q2 results showed a 23% year-on-year profit jump. However, not all earnings were celebrated—MCX slumped 7% despite a 50% annual gain. Market breadth remained positive, with defensive sectors like FMCG and pharma showing modest gains of 1.5% and 0.4% respectively.

us.headline: US markets mixed as tech gains offset Apple's earnings miss and financial weakness.
us.lead: US markets mixed as tech gains offset Apple's earnings miss and financial weakness.
us.brief: S&P 500 rose 0.36%, Nasdaq climbed 0.83%, but Dow fell 0.38% on sector rotation.
why: Tech sector surged 1.3% despite Apple's 2% drop—Nasdaq outperformance driven by AI enthusiasm from Anthropic's 1,100% revenue jump and Meta's $25 billion AI spending commitment.
Financial and Energy sectors declined 0.6% and 0.8% respectively, pulling down Dow as investors rotated away from traditional sectors.
Apple's weaker gross margin outlook and slowing services growth disappointed markets expecting stronger profitability from the mega-cap tech leader.
AI infrastructure spending dominance—Meta and AMD's massive commitments signal sustained capital outlay in artificial intelligence, attracting growth investors.
us.narrative:
US stock markets delivered a mixed verdict on 4 November 2026, with the Nasdaq 100 outperforming after a 0.83% climb while the Dow Jones fell 0.38%. The S&P 500 split the difference, rising 0.36%. Tech stocks led gains with a 1.3% sector jump, fueled by Anthropic's stunning 1,100% revenue surge ahead of its IPO and Meta's announcement of a $20–25 billion debt raise to fund AI infrastructure expansion. However, Apple's 2% post-earnings decline—triggered by guidance that signaled weaker profit margins and slowing services revenue—tempered optimism among the market's biggest names.

Beyond mega-cap drama, rotation played a key role. Healthcare slipped 0.3%, Financials dipped 0.6%, and Energy fell 0.8%, as investors favored AI and growth over defensive and cyclical plays. In India, Fractal Analytics rallied 12% after Q2 results showing net profit surge of 139% and revenue crossing ₹100 crore, underscoring appetite for homegrown AI software plays. The broader mood remained risk-on but selective: strength in AI infrastructure bets clashed with caution around traditional profitability signals from established tech giants.

tiles.sub: Revenue jumped 1,100% ahead of IPO—reshaping AI investment narrative.

tiles.sub: Massive AI infrastructure spending reflects sector's capital intensity.

tiles.sub: AI euphoria vs. profit-taking in mega-cap tech.
